newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $0.50-trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower amid light packer demand on New Year's Eve, livestock dealers said.
"There won't be much demand because everybody pretty much has the hogs they need for Tuesday," one Illinois buyer said.
"If there's any demand, it could be for start-up hogs for Thursday or Friday," he said.

Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Iowa and southern Minnesota could be steady-$0.50 lower and range from $53.50 to $54.50. Illinois top prices for hogs at the plant were expected steady from $54.00 to $54.50.
Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Indiana/Ohio were seen steady to $0.50 lower and could range from $53.50 to $54.00, the livestock dealers said.

Weakness could be pared by spillover strength from pork complex futures at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, which were up daily trading limits following Friday's bullish USDA quarterly hog inventory report, market sources said.
The report showed four percent fewer U.S. hogs as of December 1 than a year ago and showed farmers were not rebuilding herds.
